title_en: International Overseas Chinese Company v. Changjiang Film Industry Company — dispute over film distribution rights licensing contract
keywords_en: civil; contract dispute; copyright licensing contract dispute; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Guangdong Province; Jiangsu Province; legal person; Copyright Law; General Principles of the Civil Law; validity of contract; impact of distribution license on contract validity; determination and compensation for underreported box office revenue; partial support; film distribution license; box office revenue sharing; underreporting of box office revenue; good faith; copyright; film distribution licensing contract dispute
full_text_en:
Overseas Chinese Investment Corporation v. Yangtze River Film Industry Co., Ltd.

— Dispute over film distribution license contract

[Ruling Summary]

A film copyright owner may, in accordance with the provisions of the Copyright Law, exercise its copyright itself or license others to exercise its copyright. In a film copyright license contract, an agreement between the copyright owner and another party on revenue sharing in proportion and liability for breach of contract damages shall be deemed valid if it does not violate the prohibitive provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law or other relevant administrative regulations.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2001) Min San Zhong Zi No. 3

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): Guangzhou International Overseas Chinese Investment Corporation, domiciled at 21/F, Guozi Mansion, No. 363 Dongfeng Zhonglu, Guangzhou City.

Legal Representative: Luo Guangsheng, Manager of the Corporation.

Agent ad litem: Qiu Shengming, Lawyer of Guangdong Jiasite Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Feng Jun, Lawyer of Guangzhou Zhengping Tiancheng Law Firm.

Appellant (defendant at first instance): Jiangsu Yangtze River Film Industry Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 2 Huaihai Road, Nanjing City.

Legal Representative: Li Shixing, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Guo Xiaohe, Lawyer of Beijing Zhengping Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Gu Yongzhong, Lawyer of Tianda Law Firm.

With respect to the dispute over the film distribution license contract between the plaintiff at first instance Guangzhou International Overseas Chinese Investment Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the Investment Corporation) and the defendant at first instance Jiangsu Yangtze River Film Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Yangtze River Company), both the Investment Corporation and the Yangtze River Company appealed against the civil judgment (1999) Su Zhi Chu Zi No. 4 rendered by the Jiangsu High People's Court, and filed appeals to this Court. After acceptance, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, composed of Luo Dongchuan, Deputy Chief Judge of the Third Civil Trial Division, as Presiding Judge, Judge Wang Yongchang, and Acting Judge Zhang Hui. The case was heard in open court on March 28, 2001, and thereafter, on December 3, 4, 11, and 20, 2001, the parties were organized to verify the evidence. The court record was kept by Clerk Wang Yanfang. Luo Guangsheng, the legal representative of the Investment Corporation, and its agents ad litem Qiu Shengming and Feng Jun, as well as the agents ad litem of the Yangtze River Company, Guo Xiaohe and Gu Yongzhong, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial:

(1) Regarding the conclusion of the contract and its contents. In August 1997, the Investment Corporation entered into an agreement with Nanjing Film Studio, stipulating that the two parties would jointly produce the film "Next Life We Will Still Be Mother and Son" (hereinafter referred to as the "N" film), with the copyright belonging to the Investment Corporation, and Nanjing Film Studio responsible for reviewing and approving the script of the "N" film and reporting it to the competent authorities and the State Film Bureau for record. Nanjing Film Studio holds a "Film Production License." In May 1998, the Investment Corporation and the Yangtze River Company reached an oral agreement after negotiation, stipulating that the Investment Corporation would license the Yangtze River Company to distribute and exhibit the "N" film in 13 cities of Jiangsu Province. The relevant terms of the agreement are as follows: 1. The exhibition period of the "N" film in Jiangsu was from May 1998 to the end of December of the same year. 2. The box office revenue of the film would be shared between the parties in proportion. 3. The Yangtze River Company was required to fax the "Daily Exhibition Results Report" to the Investment Corporation by the morning of the day following the premiere, submit financial statements to the Investment Corporation within three days after the end of each week, and remit the Investment Corporation's share of the distribution revenue to the designated account by wire transfer within two weeks after the release, and remit all of the Investment Corporation's share within one week after the end of the distribution period. 4. The Yangtze River Company was required to verify the authenticity of the box office revenue of the "N" film reported by the film companies and theaters at the city and county levels. If the Investment Corporation discovered that theaters or companies distributing and exhibiting the "N" film had underreported or concealed box office revenue, the Yangtze River Company would bear economic compensation liability to the Investment Corporation at 10 times the amount of the underreported or concealed box office revenue. In April 1999, the Investment Corporation and the Yangtze River Company signed a written "Film Box Office Revenue Sharing Distribution and Exhibition Contract," confirming the oral agreement of May 1998 and further reaching a consensus on the proportion of box office revenue sharing, stipulating that the Investment Corporation would receive 32% and the Yangtze River Company 68%.

It was also found that Article 3 of the "Interim Provisions on Film Transactions" issued by the Ministry of Radio, Film and Television in 1995 stipulates: "Any seller participating in film transactions must hold a production or distribution license issued by the government administrative department." The Investment Corporation did not hold a production license or distribution license issued by the government administrative department.

(2) Regarding the performance of the contract by the Yangtze River Company. From May to the end of December 1998, the Yangtze River Company distributed and exhibited the "N" film in Jiangsu Province. In January 1999, based on the "Daily Exhibition Results Report" and "Exhibition Revenue Settlement Statements" of the "N" film reported by the film companies at the city and county levels in Jiangsu Province, the Yangtze River Company compiled the "Performance Index Analysis Table for Shared Films in Jiangsu Province" and the "Cumulative Performance Analysis Table for Jiangsu Province," and calculated the total box office revenue for the "N" film in the province to be RMB 1,337,081.40. In the same month, the Yangtze River Company submitted these two summary reports, along with some of the "Exhibition Revenue Settlement Statements" and "Daily Exhibition Results Reports" submitted by cities and counties, to the Investment Corporation. Later, some city and county film companies submitted supplementary box office revenue, which the Yangtze River Company calculated as RMB 40,012, but it did not inform the Investment Corporation of this supplementary revenue. During the trial of the case by the court of first instance, after verifying the various reports mentioned above, it was found that due to errors in the self-retention proportions of some city and county film companies, the Yangtze River Company had back-calculated some of the box office revenues, resulting in a discrepancy between the total box office revenue calculated by the Yangtze River Company and the total box office revenue actually reported by the cities and counties. A total of 45 cities and counties across the province reported box office revenue, with the total actually reported being RMB 1,389,190.40, which included both student and adult ticket revenue. The difference between the total box office revenue of RMB 1,337,081.40 reported by the Yangtze River Company to the Investment Corporation and the total box office revenue of RMB 1,389,190.40 actually reported by the cities and counties was RMB 52,109. Of this amount, RMB 9,429 was not included by the Yangtze River Company in the total box office revenue, but the relevant city and county reports had been submitted to the Investment Corporation. The Yangtze River Company paid a total of RMB 150,000 in distribution share to the Investment Corporation in November 1998 and April 1999. On June 28, 1999, the Yangtze River Company sent a letter to the Investment Corporation stating that the total box office revenue for the "N" film in Jiangsu was RMB 1,337,081.40, that the Investment Corporation was entitled to RMB 387,937.20, that the Yangtze River Company had already paid RMB 150,000, and that the remaining RMB 237,937.20 would be paid in full by the end of October 1999. Upon receipt of this letter, the Investment Corporation filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance on July 6, 1999.

(3) Regarding the evidence presented by the Investment Corporation and the verification conducted by the court. During the litigation, the Investment Corporation submitted to the court of first instance 1,095 questionnaires filled out by schools in Jiangsu Province. Upon investigation, it was found that the questionnaires originated from a survey activity initiated by sending letters to primary and secondary schools across the province by the relevant department. The purpose of the survey was to assist the National Coordination Committee for Film and Television Education of Primary and Secondary School Students in researching the viewing situation of the "N" film by students and parents in Jiangsu Province. The questionnaires contained a column for movie ticket revenue and required the respondents to specify the ticket revenue. Of the 1,095 questionnaires, more than 300 were filled out by schools and mailed directly to the designated location, while the remainder were collected by agents of the Investment Corporation from various schools, and in some cases, the schools were asked to fill in as high a ticket revenue amount as possible. Upon review, it was found that the questionnaires from 15 schools in Hai'an County were excluded from relevance to this case based on the viewing time, and this was also confirmed by the court of first instance's investigation of some of those schools; thus, these 15 pieces of evidence had no probative value for the facts of this case. The remaining 1,080 questionnaires involved schools distributed across 60 cities and counties in the province. Through investigations commissioned by the court of first instance to relevant courts, its own investigations, letters of inquiry, and the Yangtze River Company's acknowledgment of 18 questionnaires, the viewing situation and ticket revenue amounts for 852 schools were confirmed, while for 228 schools, due to reasons such as school closure, transfer of personnel, inability to find original records, or other reasons, the actual viewing situation or actual ticket revenue amounts could not be determined. The court of first instance compared the verified viewing situation of the 852 schools with the questionnaires submitted by the Investment Corporation, with the following results: 282 schools were confirmed not to have watched the film; for 430 schools, the ticket revenue was less than that stated in the questionnaires; for 79 schools, the ticket revenue was equal to that stated in the questionnaires; and for 61 schools, the ticket revenue was greater than that stated in the questionnaires. The total ticket revenue for the 852 schools as verified by the court was RMB 1,134,699.85, while the amount claimed by the Investment Corporation for the corresponding schools was RMB 2,751,178.10, with the court-verified amount accounting for approximately 41% of the Investment Corporation's claimed amount. The court of first instance compared the ticket revenue of the 852 schools with the ticket revenue reported by the city and county film companies, with the following results: The court found that in six counties — Jiangning, Dantu, Hongze, Huai'an, Lianshui, and Donghai — there were student ticket revenues of RMB 29,088.20, but the six county film companies did not report any ticket revenue; the court found that the student ticket revenues in 19 cities and counties — Changshu, Wuxian, Zhangjiagang, Jiangyin, Xishan, Jintan, Wujin, Danyang, Yangzhong, Yangzhou, Jiangdu, Jianhu, Jinhu, Lianyungang, Suqian (including Suyu), Sihong, Jingjiang, Taixing, and Xinghua — exceeded the total of student and adult ticket revenues reported by those 19 city and county film companies by RMB 231,892.65.

The court of first instance held that:

(1) Regarding the validity of the contract. The contract signed between the Investment Corporation and the Yangtze River Company is a film distribution license contract, which is legally valid. The Yangtze River Company argued that the contract is invalid because the Investment Corporation did not have a distribution license. The court of first instance held that the copyright in the "N" film lawfully owned by the Investment Corporation is protected by the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China. The purpose of the provision in the "Interim Provisions on Film Transactions" requiring the seller in a film transaction to hold a production or distribution license is to ensure the state's intervention and control over the production and distribution of films. In this case, although the Investment Corporation did not have a film production or distribution license, it was merely an intermediary link between the film producer and the distributor, and did not directly engage in film production or distribution itself. The production of the "N" film was carried out by Nanjing Film Studio, which held a production license, so the production link was under state control; the licensed distributor of the "N" film, the Yangtze River Company, held a distribution license, so the distribution link could also be under state control. Therefore, the Investment Corporation's act of signing the contract did not violate the spirit of the "Interim Provisions on Film Transactions." Accordingly, the Yangtze River Company's argument that the contract is invalid is not sustainable.

(2) Regarding the determination of the existence of underreporting or concealment and the amount of underreported or concealed ticket revenue. The difference between the total ticket revenue for the "N" film reported by the Yangtze River Company to the Investment Corporation and the total ticket revenue actually reported by the cities and counties was RMB 52,109. The amount of RMB 9,429 is not considered underreporting, for the following reason: Although the Yangtze River Company did not include this RMB 9,429 in the total ticket revenue, it had submitted the relevant city and county reports to the Investment Corporation, and the Investment Corporation could have identified the underreporting upon verification. This RMB 9,429 should be deemed as not having been included in the commission calculation, and the Yangtze River Company shall pay a commission of RMB 2,771 to the Investment Corporation. The remaining RMB 42,680, which the Yangtze River Company neither included in the total ticket revenue nor submitted to the city and county reports, shall be deemed as underreported or concealed ticket revenue by the Yangtze River Company. Based on the facts verified by the court regarding 852 schools, the unreported box office revenue of RMB 29,088.20 in six counties including Jiangning, and the RMB 231,892.65 in 19 cities and counties including Changshu that exceeded the box office revenue reported by the film companies, totaling RMB 260,980.85, shall be deemed as underreported or concealed ticket revenue by the city and county film companies. Since some of the 1,080 schools could not be investigated for various reasons or the ticket revenue could not be determined, and the comparison of underreporting or concealment made by the court was between the verified student ticket revenue and the total student and adult ticket revenue reported by the cities and counties, it should be reasonably presumed that the relevant cities and counties additionally underreported or concealed ticket revenue of RMB 50,000. Based on the above, the Yangtze River Company's underreporting or concealment of RMB 42,680, the verified underreporting or concealment by cities and counties of RMB 260,980.85, and the presumed underreporting or concealment by cities and counties of RMB 50,000, totaling RMB 353,660.85, it shall be determined that the Yangtze River Company has breached the contract. Therefore, the Investment Corporation's claim that the Yangtze River Company has breached the contract is established. The Investment Corporation argued that the underreported or concealed ticket revenue in Jiangsu Province amounted to several million yuan, but the 1,095 questionnaires it submitted were neither corroborated by original invoices nor consistent with the factual circumstances verified by the court, and thus cannot be used as valid evidence. Its claimed amount of underreporting or concealment cannot be established due to insufficient evidence.

(3) Regarding the liability for breach of contract for underreported or concealed ticket revenue. The Yangtze River Company's act of underreporting or concealing ticket revenue constitutes a breach of contract and shall bear liability for breach of contract. The Yangtze River Company argued that the liability for underreporting or concealment should be borne by the parties that committed the underreporting or concealment. In this regard, the court held that although the underreporting or concealment of ticket revenue was primarily committed by the city and county film companies, making it objectively difficult for the Yangtze River Company to supervise, according to Article 4, Item 6 of the contract signed between the Investment Corporation and the Yangtze River Company, this liability shall still be borne by the Yangtze River Company. With respect to the Investment Corporation's request that the Yangtze River Company bear economic compensation at 10 times the amount, the court held that the contract stipulated a 10-fold compensation for underreported or concealed ticket revenue discovered by the Investment Corporation, but the amount of underreporting or concealment provided by the Investment Corporation was not truthful and involved fraudulent conduct; the actual amount of underreporting or concealment in this case was discovered by the court, not by the Investment Corporation; moreover, applying a 10-fold compensation in this case would not be consistent with the principle of compensating actual losses under the Contract Law. Therefore, the request for 10-fold compensation was not supported. Given that the Yangtze River Company should indeed bear liability for breach of contract, based on the principle of fairness, the amount of economic loss compensation was determined at 5 times the underreported or concealed ticket revenue, i.e., 5 times the amount of RMB 353,660.85 found by the court, totaling RMB 1,768,304.25.

(4) Regarding the determination of delayed payment and liability for breach of contract. The specific proportion of the share of the "N" film between the Investment Corporation and the Yangtze River Company was agreed upon in April 1999. According to the payment deadline stipulated in the "Film Box Office Revenue Sharing Distribution and Exhibition Contract," the latest date for the Yangtze River Company to pay the entire distribution share should have been May 7, 1999. After the deadline, the Yangtze River Company still owed RMB 237,937.20 and subsequently proposed a change in the payment schedule without obtaining the Investment Corporation's consent. Therefore, the Investment Corporation's claim that the Yangtze River Company's delay in payment constituted a breach of contract is established, and the Yangtze River Company shall pay the unpaid amount of RMB 237,937.20 to the Investment Corporation.

(5) The Yangtze River Company's acts of underreporting or concealing ticket revenue and delaying payment constitute a breach of contract but do not constitute infringement. The Investment Corporation's request for a public apology from the Yangtze River Company lacks a legal basis and is not supported.

In summary, some of the Investment Corporation's claims were established, and the court supported them. In accordance with Article 10 and Article 47 of the original Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 4 and Article 111 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 128 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the following judgment: (1) The Yangtze River Company shall pay the Investment Corporation economic loss compensation of RMB 1,768,304.25. (2) The Yangtze River Company shall pay the Investment Corporation a commission of RMB 2,771. (3) The Yangtze River Company shall pay the Investment Corporation the unpaid amount of RMB 237,937.20. The above payments shall be made in full within thirty days from the effective date of this judgment. (4) The Investment Corporation's other claims are dismissed. The court acceptance fee of RMB 86,199.69 shall be borne by the Investment Corporation in the amount of RMB 46,199.69 and by the Yangtze River Company in the amount of RMB 40,000.

The Investment Corporation, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to this Court, arguing: (1) The court of first instance erred in determining the amount of box office revenue concealed by the Yangtze River Company. (a) The method used by the court of first instance to determine the concealed amount was erroneous. The RMB 1,134,699.85 in ticket revenue verified by the court of first instance was merely the box office revenue from student group viewings at 852 schools in Jiangsu Province and was not comparable to the box office revenue from adult viewers across the province reported by the Yangtze River Company. The proper handling of this case requires ascertaining the total box office revenue for the "N" film in the entire province and then comparing it with the figures reported by the Yangtze River Company to determine whether the Yangtze River Company engaged in concealment and the specific amount concealed. (b) The conclusions of the investigation conducted by the court of first instance are not accurate and are insufficient to overturn the evidence submitted by the Investment Corporation. The court of first instance merely conducted verification within the scope of the 1,095 school questionnaires provided by the Investment Corporation, and the conclusions drawn are insufficient to serve as a basis for the judgment. Moreover, the investigation data of the court of first instance were primarily based on oral or written statements from the subjects of investigation, raising questions about the objectivity of the evidence. (c) The method by which the court of first instance compiled the investigation materials and determined the ticket revenue figures was seriously unfair to the Investment Corporation. The fact that the viewing times for 15 schools in Hai'an County did not match can only suggest that the Yangtze River Company or its subordinate units had the suspicion of distributing and exhibiting the "N" film beyond the contracted period, but this cannot reduce the amount of concealment by the Yangtze River Company. The court of first instance's presumption of RMB 50,000 for the ticket revenue from schools that could not be verified and from adult viewers lacks factual and legal basis. The Yangtze River Company had a contractual obligation to ensure the accuracy of the figures it provided to the Investment Corporation; therefore, the RMB 9,429 that the court of first instance held was not concealed should be included in the Yangtze River Company's concealed amount. The conclusions of the investigation stated in the judgment of the court of first instance contradict the verification results filed in the record. The court of first instance had no reason not to adopt the evidence submitted by the Investment Corporation as Exhibit 11, and failed to verify evidence and leads that directly supported the Investment Corporation's claims, thereby artificially narrowing the scope of the Yangtze River Company's concealment. (2) The court of first instance's determination of the Yangtze River Company's liability for concealment and the nature of its conduct was incomplete. In accordance with the Copyright Law, the Yangtze River Company's concealment violated the Investment Corporation's right to receive compensation and constituted infringement. (3) Regarding the issues of late payment penalties and the allocation of litigation costs. The judgment of first instance stated that the Investment Corporation withdrew its claims for late payment penalties and for the Yangtze River Company to bear all litigation costs during the trial, which is inconsistent with the facts. In summary, the Investment Corporation requests on appeal: (1) to reverse the original judgment; (2) to order the Yangtze River Company to pay the Investment Corporation RMB 15 million in damages for breach of contract; (3) to order the Yangtze River Company to make a public apology to the Investment Corporation for its breach of contract and infringement; (4) to order the Yangtze River Company to pay the Investment Corporation RMB 237,937.20 in film box office revenue distribution share and late payment penalties; (5) to have the Yangtze River Company bear all litigation costs of this case.

The Yangtze River Company, in its oral defense against the Investment Corporation's appeal, argued: (1) The statistics on box office revenue provided by the Yangtze River Company were true, and there was no act of underreporting or concealment. (2) It agreed with the Investment Corporation's appeal that the investigation data of the court of first instance were not true or objective. (3) The Investment Corporation's claim for RMB 15 million in damages lacked factual and legal basis. (4) The majority of the questionnaires submitted by the Investment Corporation lacked signatures from school principals or official seals, and their content was not objective. (5) The Investment Corporation engaged in fraud and lacked the capacity to be a party, and therefore, the contract in dispute was invalid, and the Yangtze River Company did not breach the contract or commit infringement.

Changjiang Company also refused to accept the first-instance judgment and appealed to this Court, alleging:
(1) The first-instance procedure violated the provisions of Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law. The Investment Company had provided 1,095 pieces of evidence in support of its claims, and there was no situation where it could not collect evidence. The first-instance court collected and created evidence on its own and rendered a judgment based on it, which violated the law.
(2) The Investment Company lacked the subject-matter qualification to transfer the right to distribute and exhibit the film "Xia" for value, and therefore the "Film Box-Office Revenue Sharing Distribution and Exhibition Contract" it signed with Changjiang Company was a void contract.
(3) The first-instance court failed to ascertain the facts during trial, and the evidence on which the judgment relied was clearly insufficient. 1. The evidence collected by the first-instance court on its own was not objective and was not recognized by either party. 2. The first-instance court's approach to data analysis, using counties as units and adopting a comparison method that favored the higher figure over the lower one, was self-contradictory and fundamentally denied the truthfulness and accuracy of its own evidence. 3. The first-instance court's presumption that Changjiang Company had underreported RMB 50,000 lacked factual and legal basis. 4. The first-instance court's finding that the appellant had underreported RMB 42,680 was erroneous.
(4) The Investment Company had not verified Changjiang Company's underreporting, nor did the Investment Company recognize the facts found by the first-instance court; the first-instance judgment went beyond the parties' contractual agreement and appeared to step into each other's shoes.
(5) The first-instance court's method of calculating damages for breach of contract was unfair. 1. The award of over RMB 1.7 million in damages was unforeseeable for Changjiang Company; even if both parties had strictly performed their contractual obligations, the Investment Company could not have obtained such huge revenue. 2. The first-instance court did not determine the damages for breach based on the Investment Company's actual losses but calculated them as five times the amount of underreporting, which was unfair and violated the law and the parties' agreement.
(6) The Investment Company induced Changjiang Company into signing the contract, causing Changjiang Company to misunderstand the purpose of contract formation, which constituted serious fraud.
(7) The Investment Company and its legal representative had, through multiple correspondence, changed the party responsible for the liability for underreporting and concealment; the first-instance court's order that Changjiang Company bear compensatory liability was erroneous.
In summary, Changjiang Company requested that the second-instance court reverse the original judgment, dismiss the Investment Company's claims, and order the Investment Company to bear the litigation costs of both the first and second instances.

The Investment Company responded orally to Changjiang Company's appeal, stating:
(1) It agreed with the first-instance court's determination of the contract's validity. As the copyright owner of the film "Xia," the Investment Company had the subject-matter qualification to enter into the contract; backdating the contract did not affect its validity.
(2) The first-instance court's collection of evidence on its own did not violate the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law.
(3) It agreed with Changjiang Company's appellate argument that the data investigated by the first-instance court were not truthful and were insufficient to serve as evidence for the judgment.
(4) Regarding damages, the parties had clearly agreed on a penalty of ten times the amount of underreporting and concealment; the relevant documents of Jiangsu Province also contained similar provisions.

This Court found the following facts upon trial:
The facts found by the first-instance judgment regarding the circumstances of contract formation and the content of the contract, the performance of the contract by Changjiang Company, and the Investment Company's submission of evidence and the court's verification of evidence were substantially accurate.

It was further found that:
In verifying the 1,080 survey forms submitted by the Investment Company, the first-instance court found that 199 schools had provided original documents such as invoices, receipts, and settlement vouchers. During the first instance, Changjiang Company submitted to the first-instance court original documents concerning ticket payments for viewing the film "Xia" at 36 other schools. Apart from the above two categories, among the survey forms provided by the Investment Company, 13 survey forms were recognized by Changjiang Company during the first instance and were consistent with the verification results of the first-instance court. Upon review, among the original documents provided by the above 199 schools, the receipt issued by the Diaopu Education Committee of Taizhou City was dated December 23, 1999, which did not fall within the performance period of the contract in dispute and was unrelated to the case; this receipt could not be used as evidence in the case. The Investment Company, during the second instance, provided the original receipt for RMB 2,800 in ticket payment for viewing the film "Xia" issued by Huangxu Cinema of Dantu County on October 19, 1998, to the Huangxu Central Primary School of Dantu County, thereby denying the original receipt provided by the Huangxu Central Primary School. Changjiang Company did not raise any objection to the authenticity of the receipt provided by the Investment Company. The original receipt was verified as genuine by this Court. The receipt provided by Guoxiang Middle School in Wuxian County, Suzhou, showed the payment date as October 16, 1998, and the payee was Guoxiang Cinema, with an additional note stating that the cinema was screening a 16mm copy of the film "Xia," which did not meet the film specifications stipulated in the contract in dispute. The Investment Company provided a certification from the Beijing Film Developing and Video Recording Technology Factory, stating that the factory was exclusively responsible for developing the 16mm copies of the film "Xia," which began in November 2000. Upon review by this Court, the above receipt should be used as evidence in the case. During the second instance, the Investment Company also additionally provided a receipt for viewing the film "Xia" from Luoyang Middle School in Wujin City, Changzhou, and provided a certification from the Office of the Coordinating Committee for Film and Television Education for Primary and Secondary School Students of the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Culture, and the State Administration of Radio, Film and Television, proving that the receipt was sent to the committee by Luoyang Middle School. This receipt was also verified as genuine by this Court.

Regarding the valid original documents involving 235 schools mentioned above, some documents indicated the title of the film "Xia," with the face amount of the document being the ticket payment for viewing the film "Xia." For the remaining documents, this Court exercised its discretion in determining the credible ticket payment amount for the film "Xia" by comprehensively considering factors such as the amount of ticket payment filled in by the schools in the first-instance court's verification forms and the number of films noted on the documents as having been viewed. Based on the original documents from 235 schools and the 13 school survey forms verified as accurate by the first-instance court, the film "Xia" was screened at 148 cinemas involving 13 cities in Jiangsu Province, including Nanjing, Suzhou, Wuxi, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, Yangzhou, Xuzhou, Yancheng, Huaiyin, Nantong, Lianyungang, Suqian, and Taizhou, as well as some counties (cities). The total credible amount of ticket payments for the film "Xia" was RMB 606,443.60.

It was further found:
Article 2, Item 2 of the "Film Box-Office Revenue Sharing Distribution and Exhibition Contract" stipulated: "The box-office revenue sharing settlement statement shall consist of financial statements (Film Exhibition Revenue Settlement Statement, Weekly Statement) and statistical statements (Daily Performance Report of Film Screenings)." Among the reports submitted by the 13 city-level film companies in Jiangsu Province to Changjiang Company regarding the film "Xia," such as the "Daily Performance Report of Film Screenings" and the "Film Exhibition Revenue Settlement Statement," except for Suzhou, Yangzhou, and Yancheng cities which did not submit the "Daily Performance Report of Film Screenings," the remaining 10 city-level film companies submitted detailed statements reflecting specific cinema box-office revenue for the urban areas or some counties/cities, and the total figures in the detailed statements matched the corresponding figures in the "Film Exhibition Revenue Settlement Statement." The "Cumulative Performance Analysis Statement for Jiangsu Province" compiled by Changjiang Company was described by Changjiang Company as an internal statistical analysis document for the company, not a formal report, and could not be used as a comparison basis for calculating underreporting and concealment. Compared with the reports submitted by the city-level film companies, the statement did not fully reflect the information in those reports, specifically: the statement combined the number of adult and student audiences and box-office revenue reported by the city-level film companies into the adult column; for some areas where detailed box-office revenue for specific cinemas was reported, the statement merged several cinemas into one for statistical purposes; for areas where the city-level film companies did not submit detailed information, the statement attributed the number of audiences and box-office revenue of a certain area to one or several cinemas. The total box-office revenue in this statement was RMB 1,323,881.40, which differed from the total box-office revenue of RMB 1,389,190.40 reported by the city-level film companies to Changjiang Company and the total box-office revenue of RMB 1,337,081.40 compiled by Changjiang Company and reported to the Investment Company.

This Court compared the ticket payment amounts from the aforementioned 148 cinemas with the reports submitted by the city-level film companies in Jiangsu Province, such as the "Daily Performance Report of Film Screenings" and the "Film Exhibition Revenue Settlement Statement" for the film "Xia," and found:
(1) For the 49 cinemas located in Nanjing, Wuxi, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, Xuzhou, Huaiyin, Lianyungang, Shuyang County, Taizhou, Taixing, Xinghua, and Jingjiang cities, the respective city-level film companies had submitted detailed box-office revenue data for specific cinemas. The comparison, conducted on a per-cinema basis, showed: 22 cinemas, including Hehai Hall, People's Theater, and No. 33 Auditorium in Nanjing; Oscar Cinema, Shuofang Cinema, and Wangzhuang Cinema in Wuxi; Red Star Cinema, Weitang Hall, Xinqiao Town Cinema, and Yaxiyana Cinema City in Changzhou; Jiaohua Club in Zhenjiang; Nongken Club and Qingjiang Film City in Huaiyin; People's Cinema and Xindian Club in Lianyungang; Yuelai Cinema in Shuyang County; Kou'an Cinema and Mei Lanfang Cinema in Taizhou; Madian Cinema and Xinshi Cultural Palace in Taixing; Anfeng Cinema and Workers' Cultural Palace in Xinghua, had not reported box-office revenue, while the ticket payment amount for these 22 cinemas totaled RMB 70,492.50. Three cinemas, including Beilei Cinema, Jiangnan Cinema, and Qunzhong Cinema in Wuxi, had reported box-office revenue, but their reported figures were RMB 10,933.00 lower than the ticket payment amounts for those three cinemas. For the remaining 24 cinemas, the ticket payment amounts were lower than the corresponding cinema box-office revenue figures reported by the respective city-level film companies.
(2) For the 27 urban areas or counties where the remaining 99 cinemas were located, the respective city-level film companies had only submitted comprehensive statistical figures for box-office revenue in those areas, without detailed box-office revenue data for specific cinemas. The comparison, conducted on a regional basis, showed: four counties, including Jiangning County, Dantu County, Huai'an County, and Donghai County, had not reported any box-office revenue, while the ticket payment amounts for these four counties totaled RMB 8,774.20. Nine counties/cities, including Zhangjiagang City, Changshu City, Kunshan City, Wuxian City, Xishan City, Jiangyin City, Yangzhong City, Yangzhou City, and Jinhu County, had reported box-office revenue, but their reported figures were RMB 94,851.50 lower than the ticket payment amounts for those nine counties/cities. For the remaining 14 areas, the ticket payment amounts were lower than the corresponding area box-office revenue figures reported by the respective city-level film companies. The total of the unreported ticket payment amounts and the portions by which the reported box-office revenue was lower than the ticket payment amounts determined by this Court amounted to RMB 185,051.20.

During the first instance, at the court session on January 26, 2000, Gan Lin, the specially authorized agent ad litem of the Investment Company, expressly waived the Investment Company's claim for overdue fines and its statement on litigation costs, without imposing any condition requiring Changjiang Company to repay by the end of 2000.

During the second instance, on March 26, 2001, the Investment Company submitted to this Court a "Application Requesting the Supreme People's Court to Directly Investigate and Collect Evidence in the Box-Office Underreporting Case," requesting that the second-instance court directly ascertain the actual underreported box-office revenue for the film "Xia" by Changjiang Company and the city and county film companies and cinemas in Jiangsu Province.

The facts determined by this Court as set forth above are supported by evidence including: the "Agreement" signed between the Investment Company and Nanjing Film Studio regarding the co-production of the film "Xia"; the "Film Box-Office Revenue Sharing Distribution and Exhibition Contract" signed between the Investment Company and Changjiang Company; the survey forms provided by the Investment Company in the first instance; the verification survey forms, investigation records, and the original documents attached to 199 of the survey forms verified by the first-instance court; the certificates and the attached 36 original documents provided by Changjiang Company in the first instance; the receipt for viewing the film "Xia" provided by the Huangxu Central Primary School of Dantu County and the receipt for viewing the film "Xia" provided by Luoyang Middle School in Wujin City, Changzhou, both provided by the Investment Company in the second instance; the "Cumulative Performance Analysis Statement for Jiangsu Province" for the film "Xia" and the "Performance Index Analysis Statement for Shared Films in Jiangsu Province" submitted by Changjiang Company to the Investment Company; the "Daily Performance Report of Film Screenings" and the "Film Exhibition Revenue Settlement Statement" for the film "Xia" submitted by the city-level film companies to Changjiang Company; the certification from the Beijing Film Developing and Video Recording Technology Factory; the certification from the Office of the Coordinating Committee for Film and Television Education for Primary and Secondary School Students of the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Culture, and the State Administration of Radio, Film and Television; and the court session records of the first-instance court dated January 26, 2000.

This Court is of the opinion that: The "Film Box-Office Revenue Sharing Distribution and Exhibition Contract" signed between the Investment Company and Changjiang Company is a film distribution license contract. The parties' intentions expressed in signing the contract and in the contract were genuine, and the content of the contract does not violate national laws or public interests; it should be legally recognized as a valid contract. During the second instance, Changjiang Company defended on the ground that the contract was void, relying on two reasons: first, the Investment Company violated the relevant provisions of the "Regulations on the Administration of Films" and the "Interim Provisions on Film Transactions" and lacked the subject-matter qualification to engage in film transactions; second, the Investment Company signed the contract with it after the screening of the film "Xia" had already ended, not for the purpose of performing the contract, and backdated the signing date, constituting fraud. Regarding this disputed issue, this Court is of the opinion: First, concerning the subject-matter qualification. There is no dispute between the parties that the Investment Company and Nanjing Film Studio signed an "Agreement" for the co-production of the film "Xia," under which the Investment Company made full investment and enjoyed the copyright and all distribution revenue of the film. According to the provisions of China's Copyright Law, a copyright owner may exercise or license others to exercise his copyright and receive remuneration in accordance with the agreement or legal provisions. As the copyright owner of the film "Xia," the Investment Company's signing of the "Film Box-Office Revenue Sharing Distribution and Exhibition Contract" with Changjiang Company, under which Changjiang Company had the exclusive right to distribute the film "Xia" within Jiangsu Province and the parties agreed to share the box-office revenue in proportion, complies with the above provisions of China's Copyright Law and does not violate the provisions of that law on copyright license contracts. Considering the characteristics of the film industry and the distribution of film works, the Investment Company's sharing distribution license is also a main method for the copyright owner of a film work to exercise its copyright and obtain a return on its investment, and is not inconsistent with the legal principle of protecting civil subjects in lawfully exercising their civil rights; it is not prohibited by the mandatory provisions of China's laws or administrative regulations. The restrictive provisions on subjects and objects in activities such as film production, distribution, exhibition, and transfer for value in the "Regulations on the Administration of Films" and the "Interim Provisions on Film Transactions" were formulated by the competent film industry authorities during the process of reforming the mechanism of China's film industry for the purpose of strengthening industry management, with the aim of further deepening reform and developing and prospering the film industry. Although the Investment Company did not hold a production license or a distribution license, it did not directly participate in production or distribution activities; the actual producer and distributor of the film "Xia" each held the corresponding licenses, and the content of the film had been reviewed and approved by the competent authorities and had a screening permit. The Investment Company's licensing of Changjiang Company to distribute the film "Xia" on a sharing basis, whether from the perspective of subject or object, did not affect the normal order of the film market, nor did it hinder the state's administrative management of the film industry, and was consistent with the development direction of the reform of the film industry mechanism. Furthermore, the "Interim Provisions on Film Transactions" is a normative document of an administrative regulation nature, not a basis clearly stipulated by law for determining the validity of a contract. Therefore, the Investment Company had the subject-matter qualification to enter into the contract involved in this case. Second, concerning the issue of fraud. The "Film Box-Office Revenue Sharing Distribution and Exhibition Contract" signed by the Investment Company and Changjiang Company in April 1999 was a confirmation of the oral agreement reached between the parties in May 1998, and at the time of signing the written contract, that oral agreement had already been performed. Both the reaching of the oral agreement and the intention to supplement the written contract were genuine expressions of will by both parties; even if the request to sign the written contract was made by the Investment Company, it cannot be deemed as fraudulent conduct. Although the parties backdated the date of contract signing, this was also recognized by Changjiang Company and was consistent with the actual circumstances of the formation and performance of the oral agreement, and did not harm the interests of Changjiang Company, nor did it harm the interests of the state, the collective, or any third party. Therefore, the backdating of the contract date cannot be considered as fraudulent conduct by the Investment Company. As for whether the Investment Company signed the written agreement for the purpose of performing the contract, this is also unrelated to the validity of the contract; even if the parties had not supplemented the written contract, the oral agreement of May 1998, which had already been performed, would still be protected by law. Therefore, Changjiang Company's defense that the "Film Box-Office Revenue Sharing Distribution and Exhibition Contract" was a void contract lacks sufficient factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

Article 4, Item 6 of the "Film Box-Office Revenue Sharing Distribution and Exhibition Contract" expressly stipulates the legal responsibilities of the signatory parties regarding the issue of liability for underreporting and concealment, mainly including two aspects: the responsible party and the amount of compensation. First, concerning the responsible party. The contract expressly stipulates that Changjiang Company is obligated to verify the truthfulness of the box-office revenue for the film "Xia" reported by each film screening unit and bears compensatory liability to the Investment Company for any underreporting and concealment of box-office revenue by each film screening unit. Changjiang Company argued for exemption from liability on the ground that the Investment Company, through multiple correspondences, had changed the party subject to the 10x compensation liability to the city-level film companies and cinemas. According to the provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law and other laws, a contract modification should be made on the basis of consensus reached through consultation, with the parties expressly agreeing on the content of the modification. Although the Investment Company had written to Changjiang Company and the city-level film companies and cinemas on several occasions, requiring Changjiang Company to urge each film screening unit to truthfully report box-office revenue and proposing a 10x fine on those who underreported or concealed, these correspondences alone cannot prove that the Investment Company and Changjiang Company had reached an agreement to change the responsible party for underreporting and concealment under the "Film Box-Office Revenue Sharing Distribution and Exhibition Contract." Therefore, it cannot be concluded that the responsible party for underreporting and concealment had been changed. Changjiang Company's above defense lacks sufficient factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it. For the underreporting and concealment of box-office revenue by each film screening unit, Changjiang Company should also bear compensatory liability to the Investment Company in accordance with the contract. Any loss it suffers as a result may be resolved separately with the actual underreporting and concealing parties. Second, concerning the amount of compensation. The contract between the parties expressly stipulates that Changjiang Company shall bear compensatory liability at 10 times the amount of underreporting and concealment found by the Investment Company. Changjiang Company argued that the principle of compensating actual losses should apply in determining its compensatory liability. In this regard, this Court opines that the agreement in the "Film Box-Office Revenue Sharing Distribution and Exhibition Contract" that Changjiang Company bears 10x economic compensatory liability does not violate any prohibitive provisions of law. At the same time, given the actual circumstances of film distribution and exhibition, it is objectively difficult for the Investment Company to prove the amount of underreporting and concealment; therefore, this 10x compensatory liability only applies to the amount of underreporting and concealment that has been verified, while the actual amount of underreporting and concealment may exceed the amount verified by the parties. Thus, this agreement is not unfair to either party and does not, in fact, violate the provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law and other laws on the principles of damages for breach of contract. Therefore, the agreement on 10x compensatory liability in the contract in this case is valid and should serve as the basis for determining Changjiang Company's liability for breach of contract due to underreporting and concealment. Changjiang Company's claim that compensation should be based on actual losses is not supported by this Court. The first-instance court set Changjiang Company's compensation amount at 5 times the amount of underreporting and concealment, which did not respect the parties' valid contractual agreement and lacked legal basis, and should be corrected.

Changjiang Company reported to the Investment Company regarding whether the box office revenue figures for the film "Xia" contained omissions or concealments, and the determination of the specific amounts of such omissions or concealments, which were the focal point of the parties' dispute and the key issue in the trial of this case. The determination of the party bearing the burden of proof in this case is a prerequisite for ascertaining the facts of the case. The Investment Company requested this Court to conduct a comprehensive investigation and collection of evidence regarding the box office revenue for the film "Xia" shown throughout Jiangsu Province. This Court does not grant this request. First, the evidence related to this fact does not fall under the category of evidence that the parties cannot collect on their own due to objective reasons. The Investment Company has already submitted to the court 1,095 investigation forms proving the omissions or concealments, indicating that such evidence is not impossible for it to collect; it is merely that, due to the broad scope of the investigation, comprehensive and accurate collection is difficult. The difficulty faced by the Investment Company in adducing evidence is something it should have foreseen when entering into the contract with Changjiang Company. Second, this evidence is also not of the type that a people's court must collect on its own due to the needs of the trial. The contract explicitly stipulates that Changjiang Company shall bear ten times the liability for compensation for the amounts of omissions or concealments discovered by the Investment Company, and the Investment Company may obtain ten times the economic compensation according to the contract. In accordance with the principle of equality of rights and obligations, the Investment Company should also bear the burden of proof as stipulated in the contract. The people's court should examine and verify the evidence submitted by the Investment Company proving the amounts of omissions or concealments, rather than performing the burden of proof on behalf of the Investment Company. The court of first instance has already examined and verified the authenticity of over 1,000 investigation forms submitted by the Investment Company. If the court of second instance were to investigate and collect other evidence beyond the scope of the Investment Company's proof, it would in fact be performing the burden of proof on behalf of the Investment Company, which not only violates the agreement between the parties but also contravenes the neutral stance of the court as a judicial organ, and is also unfair to the other party. Third, given the specific circumstances of this case and the agreement between the parties, comprehensively and accurately ascertaining the amounts of omissions or concealments is not only difficult to achieve, but also, because the agreement on ten-times compensation liability allows the Investment Company to substantially compensate its economic losses even if it cannot fully ascertain the amounts, it is also not necessary for the trial of this case.

Therefore, the evidence in this case concerning the proof of the fact of omissions or concealments of the box office revenue of the film "Xia" does not fall under the evidence that should be investigated and collected by the people's court as stipulated in Article 64, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. This Court does not support the Investment Company's application for this Court to investigate and collect evidence. According to legal provisions and the contract, the Investment Company should bear the burden of proof for the fact of omissions or concealments of the box office revenue of the film "Xia" that it asserts. The court of first instance, for the needs of the trial and in order to examine and verify the authenticity of the investigation forms provided by the Investment Company, conducted a re-examination investigation on the same scope of subjects, which did not violate legal provisions. However, the court of first instance not only admitted the evidence that had been examined and verified by the Investment Company, but also used the data listed in the re-examination investigation forms that still lacked original vouchers and could not be mutually corroborated with the investigation results of the Investment Company and Changjiang Company as the basis for determining the amounts of omissions or concealments of the film "Xia", and also presumed an unascertainable amount of omissions or concealments as RMB 50,000, which lacked legal and factual basis. Both parties appealed against the objectivity of the content of the investigation forms of the court of first instance and the legality and reasonableness of the presumption of RMB 50,000. This Court adopts the appeals of both parties on these grounds.

According to the facts found by this Court, among the 1,095 investigation forms provided by the Investment Company, the viewing times of 15 schools in Hai'an County did not match the screening time of the film "Xia" as agreed in the contract of this case. The court of first instance was correct in finding that this was unrelated to the contractual dispute of this case. Among the remaining 1,080 investigation forms, a total of 235 forms were supported by valid original vouchers, and an additional 13 forms, although lacking original vouchers, were acknowledged by Changjiang Company and verified by the court of first instance. Therefore, the above total of 248 investigation forms and their related original vouchers should serve as evidence for determining the fact of omissions or concealments in this case. The other investigation forms provided by the Investment Company constitute evidence of witness testimony. As they are not corroborated by other evidence and are inconsistent with the investigation results of Changjiang Company and the court of first instance regarding the same scope of subjects, this Court does not admit these contradictory witness testimonies. The "Jiangsu Province Screening Performance Cumulative Analysis Table" compiled by Changjiang Company is not a revenue-sharing settlement form that Changjiang Company was required to report to the Investment Company under the contract, and the box office revenue figures for each cinema and the total box office revenue listed therein do not match the reports actually submitted by municipal film companies. Therefore, it cannot serve as a basis for comparison in determining the fact of omissions or concealments. In this case, the ticket revenue amounts for the film "Xia" proven by the 248 school investigation forms and related original vouchers should be compared with the reports such as the "Daily Report of Film Screening Performance" and "Film Screening Revenue Settlement Form" for the film "Xia" submitted by municipal film companies to Changjiang Company, in order to determine the fact that local film screening units omitted or concealed the box office revenue of the film "Xia". The relevant reports submitted by Changjiang Company to the Investment Company should be compared with the reports submitted by municipal film companies to Changjiang Company, in order to further determine Changjiang Company's omissions or concealments.

According to the results of this Court's comparison, 22 cinemas and theaters including Hehai Hall in Nanjing City failed to report box office revenue totaling RMB 70,492.50; 3 cinemas and theaters including Beilei Cinema in Wuxi City reported box office revenue lower than the amount determined by this Court by RMB 10,933.00; 4 counties including Jiangning County failed to report box office revenue totaling RMB 8,774.20; and 9 counties and cities including Zhangjiagang City reported box office revenue lower than the amount determined by this Court by RMB 94,851.50. The total of the above four items is RMB 185,051.20, which should be determined as the amount of box office revenue for the film "Xia" omitted or concealed by local film screening units. The total box office revenue for the film "Xia" actually reported by municipal film companies was RMB 1,389,190.40. Changjiang Company calculated it as RMB 1,337,081.40 and conducted revenue-sharing settlement with the Investment Company based on that amount. Of the difference of RMB 52,109, Changjiang Company had already submitted reports for RMB 9,429 to the Investment Company. Although this constitutes a breach of contract, it cannot be determined as an act of omission or concealment. Changjiang Company should pay the Investment Company a commission of RMB 2,771 for this RMB 9,429 in box office revenue in accordance with the contract. The Investment Company's appeal that this RMB 9,429 should be determined as omitted or concealed ticket revenue by Changjiang Company is not supported by this Court. The remaining RMB 42,680 was not reported by Changjiang Company to the Investment Company, nor did Changjiang Company require the municipal film companies to report directly to the Investment Company. Therefore, it should be determined as the amount of omitted or concealed ticket revenue by Changjiang Company. Changjiang Company's defense that the RMB 42,680 does not constitute omissions or concealments lacks factual basis, and this Court does not support it either. The total amount of omitted or concealed ticket revenue from the above two items is RMB 227,731.20. According to the agreement in Article 4, Item 6 of the "Film Box Office Revenue-Sharing Distribution and Screening Contract", Changjiang Company should bear the liability of compensating the Investment Company for economic losses of RMB 2,277,312. In addition, Changjiang Company should pay the Investment Company the outstanding commission of RMB 237,937.20. The Investment Company waived its claim for late payment penalty during the first instance proceedings, without attaching any conditions. Therefore, Changjiang Company's liability for late payment penalty should be discharged accordingly. The Investment Company's appeal that the first instance judgment misstated the issues of late payment penalty and litigation costs lacks factual basis and cannot be sustained. Under the circumstances of concurrence of liability for breach of contract and tort, the Investment Company chose to initiate an action for breach of contract. Therefore, this Court does not support its appeal to pursue Changjiang Company's tort liability.

In summary, the first instance judgment erred in finding some facts, but its application of law was basically correct. Pursuant to Articles 10, 24, and 53 of the Copyright Law of the PRC, Article 4 and Article 111 of the General Principles of Civil Law of the PRC, and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court modifies the judgment as follows:

1. Set aside Item (1) of the Civil Judgment (1999) Su Zhi Chu Zi No. 4 of the Jiangsu High People's Court;

2. Jiangsu Changjiang Film Industry Co., Ltd. shall compensate Guangzhou International Overseas Chinese Investment Company for economic losses in the amount of RMB 2,277,312 (to be paid within 10 days after this judgment takes effect);

3. Affirm Items (2), (3), and (4) of the Civil Judgment (1999) Su Zhi Chu Zi No. 4 of the Jiangsu High People's Court.

The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 86,199.69 shall be borne by Jiangsu Changjiang Film Industry Co., Ltd.; the second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 86,199.69 shall be borne by Jiangsu Changjiang Film Industry Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 43,100 and by Guangzhou International Overseas Chinese Investment Company in the amount of RMB 43,099.69.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Luo Dongchuan

Judge: Wang Yongchang

Acting Judge: Zhang Hui
